header: Date: 2026-05-11 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 mins | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Silvercrest Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Silvercrest Platform Eng), Nadia Park (Silvercrest CTO)
summary: Redwood team walked Silvercrest through the Optimize console focusing on a hybrid KV/prefix caching strategy and batching presets to hit a 95th percentile latency target while reducing token cost. Discussed tradeoffs (prefetch vs sessionized KV) and net savings scenarios in the cost-simulator. Agreed to provide sandbox config, security pack, and run a 48-hour benchmark with customer traces.
topics: Dynamic batching strategies and batch size heuristics
Prefix vs KV/session cache tradeoffs and hybrid approach
Security constraints (VPC, KMS, SOC2) and private deployments
Pilot plan and benchmark next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya Chen from Redwood, AE. We got Raj from SE side, and on the Silvercrest side can you all confirm attendees?
[00:09] Alicia: Yeah hi, Alicia here, Head of ML at Silvercrest. Tom's on from infra and Nadia is here as well.
[00:16] Maya: Awesome, quick agenda: we'll show the Optimize console, run a couple cost sims with your session profiles, dig into prefix vs KV caching and a hybrid pattern we've seen work, then recap next steps. Sound good?
[00:28] Tom: Yep, sounds good. We're most curious about hitting <120ms P95 and dropping per-token cost.
[00:35] Raj: Great — I'll kick off in the console, but quick note: some names get munged in the transcript — when I say KV cache you might see K V or K-V in the notes.
[00:44] (crosstalk)
[00:47] Raj: Ok opening Optimize > Playbooks. So here's the pre-built batching presets, we have small/medium/large request distributions and adaptive dynamic batching. For Silvercrest workloads you told us the median prompt length is ~60 tokens with few-shot context of 120 tokens, right?
[01:05] Alicia: That's right, about 60 median, tail up to 2k for some search re-ranks but most are short.
[01:12] Raj: Good — for that distribution, static large batch sizing hurts latency at tail, so adaptive batch that caps at 8 with a micro-delay of 8ms gives good throughput without exploding P95.
[01:25] Tom: Is that the micro-delay we were worried about? If we add 8ms we're still ok? Our SLO is 120ms.
[01:32] Raj: Yes — the micro-delay is a tradeoff: it waits briefly to form batches. In our sim with your RPS profile (peak 180 rps) the median + lookahead prefetch reduces cold KV lookups.
[01:44] Maya: I'll pull up the cost-simulator sheet we shared in the deck link: https://redwood.ai/decks/silvercrest-optimize-playbook (note: internal link).
[01:52] Raj: In the simulator we model three levers: batching (effective tokens per GPU call), prefix/KV caching (hit rate), and quantization/mode (FP16 vs int8-like approximations).
[02:04] Alicia: Walk me through prefix vs KV — we've used sessionization in-house but not a full KV cache.
[02:11] Raj: Sure — prefix cache is cheap when many requests share beginning tokens — think initial prompt scaffolding. KV cache (we call it sessionized KV) stores KV-cache per session so subsequent tokens skip the attention recompute; it's heavier in memory but high hit-value for multi-turn or long contexts.
[02:28] Raj: There's also a hybrid approach: prefetch likely prefixes into a shared prefix store and keep hot sessions in KV with TTL. That limits RAM while still catching most repeated tails.
[02:40] Tom: How do you quantify cost-savings? We need numbers to justify Dedicated vs hosted.
[02:46] Raj: In the sim we take your RPS, token lengths, and run scenarios: baseline (no cache, naive batching), prefix-only, KV-only, hybrid. For Silvercrest with the provided RPS and 25% session reuse, the prefix-only saves ~18-25% token compute; KV-only saves ~28-40% depending on hit rate, hybrid nails around 35-45% with careful TTLs.
[03:07] Nadia: Hit rates are the thing — our reuse is bursty across users, are there best practices to tune TTLs?
[03:14] Raj: Yes — use sliding TTLs tied to session affinity. Start with TTL = 30 minutes for hot sessions, then decay to 5 minutes for broader sessions. Also use eviction policies by frequency. The Optimize console can simulate those hit rates if you upload traces.
[03:29] Maya: (brief) I want to call out a common mis-hear in notes: when we say 'KV' sometimes shows as 'K V' so the exported CSV has that noise.
[03:35] Alicia: haha noted. So what's the impact on P95 when enabling prefetch?
[03:40] Raj: Prefetch reduces first-token latency for common prefixes, so P95 moves down if the first-token dominates. But prefetch itself consumes bandwidth and can increase concurrent memory usage. In our sandbox run with similar search patterns, prefetch + adaptive batching met 110ms P95 and reduced token cost by 38%.
[03:58] Tom: What about memory on Dedicated instances — do we need more GPUs?
[04:03] Raj: For KV-heavy workloads, yes you need memory headroom. We model memory per-GPU and recommend either larger instance types or sharded KV across GPU pools. Dedicated gives you easier predictability; hosted can auto-fallback to cheaper variants but might not guarantee tail SLOs for enterprise SLAs.
[04:21] Alicia: We care a lot about data controls — VPC and KMS. Does Optimize change anything about that?
[04:26] Maya: No, Optimize is just a control plane/console. For Private deployments or Dedicated we can enable VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs. We'll include the security pack with the AOC.
[04:36] Tom: Great. Anything in the sim that caught your eye as risky?
[04:40] Raj: One risk is optimistic hit-rate assumptions. If your session reuse drops <10%, KV costs (memory + management) may not pay off. That's why we recommend a short 48h pilot with real traces.
[04:51] Alicia: Ok — so we run a pilot, get real hit rates, then decide TTL and batch presets.
[04:56] Raj: Exactly. I'll demo uploading a trace now — going to Optimize > Traces > Upload. (typing noises)
[05:05] Raj: The console accepts gzipped JSON of session traces; we map session_id, prompt tokens, response tokens, latency. For privacy we can hash user IDs client-side.
[05:14] Tom: We'll hash before sending. What about model variants? We sometimes prefer a smaller quantized model for background ranking.
[05:20] Raj: Optimize supports model routing policies — you can route by cost or latency budget. For background ranking route to a quantized 8-bit variant; for user-facing chat route to FP16. The console sim will show mix cost/latency.
[05:33] Maya: I'm jumping to the Cost Simulator tab — here's the scenario dropdown: baseline, prefix-only, kv-only, hybrid, dedicated-reserved. We can tweak concurrency, batch windows, and hit rates.
[05:44] (screen share silence while Raj manipulates sliders)
[06:00] Raj: Now I'm increasing your RPS to simulate spikes at 350 rps — hybrid still holds better cost curve vs kv-only in the mid-range. But at very high scale, dedicated reserved capacity with autoscaling bursts can beat hosted on per-token unit cost.
[06:16] Tom: Any hard numbers for reserved? We have rough budget ceiling.
[06:20] Maya: We'll send a few sample commit tiers in the pricing sheet, but ballpark reserved can drop unit costs 20-35% depending on commit and prefetch efficacy.
[06:29] Alicia: For the pilot, what's minimal instrumentation we need?
[06:33] Raj: 1) session traces (7 days), 2) RPS histogram, 3) target latency SLOs, 4) a small subset of policies you want to test (e.g., prefix TTL 10/30/60m). With that we can run the 48h sim and give recommendations.
[06:47] Tom: We can do that. One more question: is the streaming token cost different with KV caches?
[06:53] Raj: Streaming cost per-token remains, but KV reduces tokens that need recomputation (less encoder/decoder steps), so effective billed compute reduces. The console shows effective tokens per request after caching.
[07:05] (brief pause)
[07:08] Alicia: There were some glossary mismatches in our internal notes — can you put a short doc that maps terms (prefix cache vs session KV vs prefetch)?
[07:14] Maya: Yes, we'll attach a 1-pager.
[07:17] Raj: Back to the sim — now toggling prefetch aggressiveness. If we prefetch frequently the hit-rate rises but so does background IO. For Silvercrest I recommended conservative prefetch with higher TTLs on hot sessions.
[07:31] Tom: Does the console support sampling rules? We don't want prefetch for low-value requests.
[07:36] Raj: Yes you can define sampling rules by route, user cohort, or metadata. The Playbooks tab lets you associate a policy with a named route.
[07:45] Nadia: On security again, we need audit trails for token access per-route — is that available?
[07:50] Maya: Yes, audit logs per-route and per-token-level cost breakdown is in Redwood Console. For Private we can retain logs in your S3 or log archive for compliance.
[07:59] Alicia: Good. Let's talk about edge cases: long retrievals with 2k context — does KV handle that?
[08:06] Raj: KV helps because it avoids recomputing earlier layers for repeated generation, but memory grows. For long contexts, a prefix store + sharded KV is typically better than full in-memory KV for all sessions. The console sim will show memory utilization per-GPU under each pattern.
[08:21] Tom: We're concerned about cold-start cost when traffic shifts suddenly. Any mitigations?
[08:26] Raj: Warm pools and pre-warmed prefix caches can ameliorate cold-starts. Also use auto-fallback to a smaller model temporarily while warming KV caches.
[08:36] Alicia: Could you run a quick 'what-if' — 30% drop in session reuse, what's the delta?
[08:41] Raj: (typing) Ok sim loaded... with reuse at 30% hybrid drops to ~22% saving vs baseline, KV-only drops more dramatically. Numbers in the sheet: baseline cost X, hybrid Y (22% reduction). I'll export the CSV after this call.
[09:02] Maya: Quick pause for clarifying question from Tom on dedicated burst capacity billing.
[09:08] Tom: If we reserve, do bursts cost more on top of commit?
[09:12] Maya: Bursts are metered; we include burst credits in some tiers, otherwise bursts are billed at a pre-agreed overage. We'll send specifics.
[09:19] (small side discussion about procurement timelines)
[09:30] Raj: Returning to settings — here's a sample playbook we've used for fintech: prefix TTL 20m, KV hot TTL 45m, adaptive batch max 12, micro-delay 10ms, sampling rule to exclude low-value ETL routes. This achieved consistent P95 under 100ms in our sandbox.
[09:48] Alicia: That looks promising. Any gotchas about tokenization differences causing mismatched prefix hits?
[09:54] Raj: Yes — tokenization mismatch can reduce prefix hit rates; we recommend canonicalizing prompts server-side and stripping variable user tokens before storing prefixes. The console has a normalization step you can enable.
[10:07] Tom: For the pilot, will Redwood host the sandbox or do we need to spin up private infra?
[10:12] Maya: We can host a sandbox in Redwood hosted environment with a shared test tenant, or we can configure a private sandbox in your VPC if you prefer. For quick iteration hosted sandbox is easiest.
[10:22] Nadia: We prefer hosted initially but want to review the audit logs and data retention policies.
[10:27] Maya: We'll include the retention config in the security pack.
[10:30] (silence while Raj pulls up export)
[10:45] Raj: Exporting current sim... attaching CSV to chat: https://redwood.ai/sandbox-exports/ff-5421-silvercrest-sim1.csv
[10:54] Alicia: Thanks. A practical question: what's the monitoring we get post-rollout to catch regressed quality when using quantized models?
[11:02] Raj: Optimize ties to the Evals and Alerts framework — you can set regression checks on prompt sets and the console will alert if NLL or BLEU-ish metrics degrade beyond threshold. Also keep an evaluation harness in CI to gate new quantized variants.
[11:18] Tom: Nice. One more — how do rate limits interact with batching? If rate limiter caps, batching could starve.
[11:25] Raj: Good point — rate limiter works at gateway; batching happens in the serving runtime. We recommend coordinating rate limiters to allow short bursts for batching windows, otherwise batching headroom is limited. There's a policy flag in Console to allow batch windows to bypass soft rate limits.
[11:40] Maya: We have about 40 minutes left in the call — any other deep dive requests?
[11:45] Alicia: Can we see memory utilization charts for hybrid vs KV-only?
[11:49] Raj: Yes — switching to Observability > Simulated Utilization. (typing) Here: KV-only uses ~2.4x memory vs hybrid at peak, hybrid spreads across prefix store and smaller per-session KV.
[12:05] Tom: That makes sense. On the hybrid pattern, what's the recommended shard count for our scale?
[12:10] Raj: For peak 350 rps and 12 max batch, start with 4 shards across GPU pool and monitor. We can autoscale shards if you go dedicated.
[12:20] Alicia: How durable is the prefix store? If we lose a shard during deploy, do we recalc from scratch?
[12:26] Raj: Prefix store is replicated with eventual consistency; losing a shard increases cold-start lookups but it's not catastrophic. We replicate hot items across shards to avoid single-point failures.
[12:37] (brief interruption — someone's connection hiccup)
[12:45] Raj: Wrapping towards pilot logistics — we'll need traces and a small test route. We'll perform the 48-hour benchmark and return a recommended playbook and expected cost delta.
[12:56] Tom: Can we include a scenario that routes 20% of traffic to quantized background model?
[13:01] Raj: Absolutely — include it in the trace metadata or we'll add a synthetic route for the sim.
[13:10] Maya: Quick recap: Redwood to send security pack + pricing + 1-pager glossary; Raj to share sandbox + sim export; Silvercrest to upload traces; plan pilot for week of May 25.
[13:23] Alicia: Sounds good. Any blockers from our side?
[13:27] Nadia: We'll need legal to confirm data-sharing for traces but hashing should cover it.
[13:33] Maya: We'll make the trace upload guidance explicit in the email.
[13:36] (call winds down, casual sign-offs)
[13:45] Tom: Thanks all, talk soon.
[13:47] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts.
[13:50] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: some terms were auto-transcribed oddly (K V, pre-fetch as prefetch vs pre-fetch) and proper nouns (Silvercrest sometimes seen as Silver Crest). Exports attached were short links above.
